overview: Alton C. Parker became the first Black police officer in his hometown in 1941, later rising to become Canada’s first Black detective. In an era marked by deep racial bias, he broke barriers within the Windsor Police Force, confronting skepticism and systemic obstacles. Through skill, resilience, and determination, he earned the respect of colleagues and the community. His journey reshaped perceptions within law enforcement and helped spark broader social change, leaving a lasting legacy of possibility.
